GOV_REFORM_ACCORD.name: Reform Accord
GOV_REFORM_ACCORD.seat_logic: Renewal Alliance 68 + Civic Labour 52 + at least one Independent = 121+
risks: Mira must prove Labour is not junior partner

GOV_RECONSTRUCTION.name: Reconstruction Coalition
GOV_RECONSTRUCTION.seat_logic: Renewal Alliance 68 + Stability Union 46 + at least seven Independents = 121+

GOV_CIVIC_COMPACT.name: Civic Compact
GOV_CIVIC_COMPACT.seat_logic: Civic Labour 52 + Stability Union 46 + Free Cities 22 + at least one Independent = 121+
risks: Adrian becomes strong opposition focal point

acts.title: THE OUTSIDER
acts.player_state: Junior analyst, SCS. Information access without command authority.
acts.world_state: Hung parliament, Harbor Contracts scandal unresolved, Aster financing clock running.
acts.central_question: Who actually has power, what is true, and which relationships are real?

chapters.title: DAY ZERO
chapters.premise: The morning after the election, the SCS receives three incompatible coalition maps before markets open.
required_beats: Player discovers that formal seat arithmetic is not enough: attendance, independents, internal party factions and procedure matter.
Mara gives the player a raw briefing task rather than a recommendation task.
Nela Orr quietly corrects a procedural assumption everyone in the political press is repeating.
chapters.decision_gate: Whether the player reports uncertainty honestly or turns a fragile inference into a confident recommendation.
delayed_consequences: Establishes the player's first credibility profile with Mara and the Presidency.
Silas receives his first weak signal that an unknown SCS analyst influenced the morning brief.

chapters.title: THE 121ST VOTE
chapters.premise: Every plausible government is one or more votes short once real commitments are separated from public statements.
required_beats: Niko Arven is treated by parties as a number; he pushes back.
The player must distinguish stated ideological objections from concrete regional demands.
Silas uses a harmless rumor to see which coalition channel reacts.
chapters.decision_gate: Which missing vote is actually obtainable without creating a future hostage relationship.
delayed_consequences: Creates early obligations to regional actors.
Can give Silas data about the player's verification and response speed.

chapters.title: THE FILE
chapters.premise: Civic Wire receives another Harbor document. Most of it is authentic; one annotation has uncertain provenance.
required_beats: Nadia asks the SCS to confirm a technical timeline.
Selma warns that public comment could compromise chain of custody.
Anton offers context that makes one suspicious meeting less simple than it looks.
chapters.decision_gate: How much the player confirms, to whom, and with what confidence language.
delayed_consequences: Nadia may come to see the player as a reliable reality-check or as another gatekeeper.
Selma's later willingness to share process information changes.

chapters.title: THE PRESIDENT'S HOUR
chapters.premise: Party leaders arrive separately at the Presidency. Everyone believes someone else has a secret deal.
required_beats: Ivo makes the player compress four pages into one decision brief.
Elena asks which statements are facts, which are beliefs, and which are bargaining positions.
Liora insists any coalition bargain involving emergency authorities must include sunset clauses.
chapters.decision_gate: What goes into the President's one-page synthesis—and what is deliberately left as uncertain.
delayed_consequences: Determines which actors believe the Presidency is neutral.
Teaches that controlling the brief can be power even without voting.

chapters.title: THE PRICE OF A MINISTRY
chapters.premise: Coalition talks move from principles to portfolios, budgets and veto rights.
required_beats: Three coalition architectures become viable.
Each ministry allocation changes not only prestige but implementation power over Aster Gate, labor, finance and security.
Silas proposes a deal that looks generous because he values a hidden procedural veto more.
chapters.decision_gate: Whether the player recognizes the difference between visible ministries and actual implementation chokepoints.
delayed_consequences: Locks coalition promises that return in Acts II–III.
Determines which faction feels under-credited even if materially satisfied.

chapters.title: GOVERNMENT AT DAWN
chapters.premise: A government must be presented before financial markets reopen after a long weekend.
required_beats: The player delivers the final coalition risk map.
Aster Gate financing and market confidence make indefinite delay costly.
The parties demand control over the strategic-coordination function.
chapters.decision_gate: Which governing configuration forms and under what constraints; whether the SCS becomes a protected cross-government office or a partisan unit.
delayed_consequences: Sets GOVERNMENT_CONFIGURATION.
Sets the founding legitimacy and autonomy of the future NSO.
The player's name becomes known to top political strategists.

acts.title: THE OPERATOR
acts.player_state: The player receives an operational portfolio; title varies by government branch.
acts.world_state: Government exists, but coalition promises now collide with implementation, financing and labor.
acts.central_question: Seeing the right move is not the same as making a system execute it.

chapters.title: THE OFFICE WITH NO ARMY
chapters.premise: The new National Strategy Office is authorized with impressive remit but almost no direct command power.
required_beats: Mara designs reporting lanes.
Ministries resist giving data to a new coordinating body.
The player must obtain cooperation without pretending to have authority they do not possess.
chapters.decision_gate: Build NSO through mandates, relationships, or personal escalation.
delayed_consequences: Determines whether NSO grows as institution, patronage node, or player-centered network.
Lea's autonomy trajectory begins.

chapters.title: NINETY-TWO DAYS
chapters.premise: Continental Compact financing for Aster Gate expires unless governance and procurement architecture is agreed.
required_beats: Emil wants milestone certainty.
Damir argues only Aureon can mobilize fast enough.
Liora and Selma warn against tailored procurement.
Alina proposes modular lots rather than one concession.
chapters.decision_gate: Choose procurement architecture that balances delivery speed, competition, coordination and capture risk.
delayed_consequences: Aureon's future leverage changes.
Construction speed and Continental financing conditions change.
Creates latent corruption/capture exposure for Act III.

chapters.title: THE MACHINE FLOOR
chapters.premise: Nexa and manufacturers announce automation plans before the labor transition framework is ready.
required_beats: Rina threatens coordinated action but privately asks for early bargaining.
Ilyan claims delay will lose a technology cycle.
Lea shows displacement is geographically concentrated rather than nationwide.
chapters.decision_gate: Design a transition package: sequencing, retraining, worker voice, productivity sharing and rollout speed.
delayed_consequences: Sets LABOUR_PACT_QUALITY.
Affects Daran stability, growth capacity and Rina/Mira trust.
Changes whether a later strike is structural or avoidable.

chapters.title: CHEAP ENERGY
chapters.premise: Ordan offers a five-year energy contract significantly below alternatives just as fiscal pressure rises.
required_beats: Avera frames the offer as ordinary commerce.
Tomas calls long lock-in strategic vulnerability.
Sofia warns expensive diversification can itself weaken the state.
Compact financing for alternatives is slower than the contract deadline.
chapters.decision_gate: Choose contract duration, diversification spend and exit/volume options.
delayed_consequences: Sets ORDAN_ENERGY_DEPENDENCY and FISCAL_HEADROOM.
Avera updates her model of what the player values.
Act V energy crisis severity becomes state-dependent.

chapters.title: SOVEREIGN CLOUD
chapters.premise: Nexa proposes the digital layer for Aster Gate while depending on foreign compute providers.
required_beats: Ilyan's sovereignty pitch is directionally true but ahead of present capability.
Liora wants auditability and privacy.
Eren worries about supply-chain access.
Aureon wants integration clarity.
chapters.decision_gate: Define architecture and procurement so Lydria gains capability without pretending current independence.
delayed_consequences: Sets DIGITAL_DEPENDENCY and NEXA_LEVERAGE.
Determines whether later cyber/compute shocks create single-point failure.

chapters.title: THE FIRST REVIEW
chapters.premise: Six months in, the government wants a public scorecard. Several reforms look better on paper than in execution.
required_beats: Ministries lobby the player to choose flattering metrics.
Vela offers prime-time interview.
Lea finds one headline KPI that is being gamed.
chapters.decision_gate: Publish a scorecard architecture and decide how much personal visibility to accept.
delayed_consequences: Sets PLAYER_VISIBILITY and INFORMATION_QUALITY.
Can make the player a public strategic figure earlier than is safe.
Silas gains more observable data if visibility is high.

acts.title: THE KINGMAKER
acts.player_state: The player's network now crosses cabinet, opposition, business, media and institutions.
acts.world_state: The first coalition's internal costs mature; Aster Gate and the Harbor investigation create redistribution fights.
acts.central_question: Every gain now costs something else that also matters.

chapters.title: WHO OWNS THE GATE?
chapters.premise: Aster Gate moves from architecture to concessions. Fast execution and anti-capture design now collide directly.
required_beats: Aureon can integrate physical infrastructure fastest.
Modular contracting reduces capture but creates coordination risk.
Foreign consortium bids threaten domestic control narratives.
chapters.decision_gate: How much infrastructure control can one operator hold, and what interoperability/exit rights are mandatory?
delayed_consequences: Sets ASTER_CHOKEPOINT_CONCENTRATION.
Determines Damir vs Alina succession leverage.
Future infrastructure crisis may be faster to solve but more dependent on Aureon.

chapters.title: THE STORY THAT WON'T DIE
chapters.premise: Selma's Harbor investigation reaches prosecutable findings while Nadia prepares a broader story about the culture that allowed them.
required_beats: The criminal case is narrower than the systemic story.
Anton can explain how crisis urgency normalized undocumented access.
Petra knows more but fears becoming the convenient villain.
chapters.decision_gate: Whether government treats the scandal as individuals, system design, or both.
delayed_consequences: Old-order legitimacy, Stability Union recovery, Selma/Nadia relationship and procurement reform all change.
Harbor ceases to be a mystery and becomes an institutional lesson—or a permanent partisan myth.

chapters.title: THE SECOND COALITION INSIDE THE FIRST
chapters.premise: Cabinet partners cooperate publicly while building rival issue coalitions around labor, data, security and regional spending.
required_beats: A nominal coalition vote no longer predicts policy votes.
The player can broker issue coalitions, but each success increases personal centrality.
Silas starts mapping which actor the player contacts first under pressure.
chapters.decision_gate: Build a cross-party solution or force discipline through the governing coalition.
delayed_consequences: Sets COALITION_ECOLOGY and PLAYER_CENTRALITY.
Determines whether the player becomes bridge or bottleneck.

chapters.title: THE HEIR
chapters.premise: Damir's health scare brings Aureon succession forward. Creditors, politicians and executives choose sides before he has.
required_beats: Alina wants governance reform.
Petra fears rapid dismantling of relationship capital.
Meridian cares about continuity more than family symbolism.
Damir interprets preparation for succession as doubt in his authority.
chapters.decision_gate: Whether the player helps broker transition, stays out, or uses the moment to restructure Aureon's public leverage.
delayed_consequences: Corporate network redistributes rather than disappears.
Alina/Damir/Petra trajectories diverge.
Aster Gate execution capacity changes.

chapters.title: ONE VOTE TOO MANY
chapters.premise: A budget/confidence package fails unless one bloc receives a concession that violates another partner's red line.
required_beats: Nela identifies a lawful sequencing option nobody considered.
Niko can supply a vote at regional cost.
Liora can abstain if transparency provision changes.
Mira must show visible distributional gain.
chapters.decision_gate: Save the existing government, redesign the package, or allow a controlled political reset.
delayed_consequences: Creates KINGMAKER_EVENT_1.
Actors begin attributing government survival/fall personally to the player.

chapters.title: THE KINGMAKER
chapters.premise: After the confidence crisis, at least two viable governing arrangements exist. Leaders privately ask the player what they should do.
required_beats: The player now has enough network information to make one coalition possible and another impossible.
Mara warns that an analyst who starts choosing governments has changed roles whether or not the title changed.
Silas offers cooperation on a government architecture that limits both players' factions.
chapters.decision_gate: Use influence to preserve, replace or reconfigure government—and decide whether to remain inside the NSO, take political appointment, or preserve institutional distance.
delayed_consequences: Locks PLAYER_POWER_ROUTE: institutional / political / network.
Sets second government configuration.
Changes Mara, Lea, Elena and Silas relationships for the rest of campaign.

acts.title: THE COUNTERPLAYER
acts.player_state: The player is now a known strategic actor. Opponents and allies model their behavior.
acts.world_state: The country's institutions are functioning, but every major actor has learned from the first two years.
acts.central_question: What happens when everyone else learns how you think?

chapters.title: THE PROBE
chapters.premise: A minor parliamentary leak seems too small to matter. Its real purpose is to observe how the player verifies and responds.
required_beats: The leak contains one harmless error and one useful truth.
Silas can plausibly observe who the player calls and how quickly.
Lea notices the pattern only if the NSO retained provenance discipline.
chapters.decision_gate: Respond normally, vary process intentionally, or investigate whether this is a probe.
delayed_consequences: Updates SILAS_MODEL confidences.
Begins explicit counterplayer phase without giving Silas omniscience.

chapters.title: TWO SOURCES
chapters.premise: Two apparently independent reports point to the same Ordan-linked financing network. Their provenance partially converges.
required_beats: Eren refuses to call domestic recipients agents.
Nadia has documents but one source chain overlaps.
Avera offers verifiable commercial explanation for part of the network.
chapters.decision_gate: How to attribute influence without overstating control.
delayed_consequences: Can preserve or damage NID legitimacy.
Affects Ordan diplomatic channel and domestic faction polarization.

chapters.title: THE RED LINE
chapters.premise: A Serrat patrol and Lydrian coast-guard vessel collide near disputed waters. No one is killed; both sides publish incompatible maps.
required_beats: Tomas needs a visible boundary.
Talia needs a face-saving path.
Niko's island constituents demand firmness.
The incident facts are less clear than the public narrative.
chapters.decision_gate: Set immediate operational posture, investigation mechanism and public message.
delayed_consequences: Sets MARITIME_HEAT.
If handled well, Talia becomes crisis counterpart later; if badly, domestic hardliners on both sides gain power.

chapters.title: THE WEDGE
chapters.premise: A foreign-backed commercial proposal gives one coalition faction a major regional benefit but undermines the government's shared strategic-autonomy plan.
required_beats: The offer is economically real, not a fake bribe.
Rejecting it imposes local cost.
Accepting it creates a dependency node and coalition status asymmetry.
chapters.decision_gate: Design compensation, conditions, or acceptance/rejection in a way that does not turn one member into a permanent wedge.
delayed_consequences: Updates ORDAN_LEVERAGE and coalition grievances.
Silas learns whether player prioritizes systemic consistency over local bargains.

chapters.title: WHO WATCHES THE OFFICE?
chapters.premise: Free Cities and Integrity Commission demand oversight after evidence that NSO briefings increasingly determine cabinet agendas.
required_beats: No proven abuse exists.
The concern is structural: agenda selection and information filtering now have political consequences.
A strong oversight design may reduce speed and player discretion.
chapters.decision_gate: Accept meaningful oversight, design cosmetic oversight, fight inquiry, or shrink NSO remit.
delayed_consequences: Sets NSO_LEGITIMACY and PLAYER_DISCRETION.
Lea/Mara relationship becomes a major legacy predictor.
Future emergency authority is easier or harder to justify.

chapters.title: THE MIRROR
chapters.premise: Silas predicts the player's likely response to a coalition maneuver and builds a second move around that adaptation.
required_beats: The first maneuver is deliberately legible.
Lea can identify one inconsistency suggesting a trap.
Silas's true objective is not necessarily to defeat the player; it may be to force a public commitment that narrows future options.
chapters.decision_gate: Use probe/mixed response, commit to the obvious counter, or refuse the frame entirely.
delayed_consequences: If player counters well, Silas respect rises and model confidence drops.
If player is exploited, the loss may be political rather than game-ending.
Act ends with recognition that strategy itself is now observable behavior.

acts.title: THE SYSTEM
acts.player_state: The player's influence is large enough that every intervention creates second- and third-order consequences.
acts.world_state: Latent vulnerabilities accumulated by earlier choices converge. The exact crisis stack is state-dependent.
acts.central_question: Can the system function when no single decision can be isolated?

chapters.title: MONDAY, 06:10
chapters.premise: The Situation Room opens with more serious problems than the player has attention to manage.
required_beats: Engine selects the three highest-pressure crisis modules from finance, energy, maritime, labor, Aster infrastructure and government stability.
Some reports conflict and some are simply late.
Player must delegate.
chapters.decision_gate: Which crises receive direct attention, who receives delegated authority, and what decision cadence is established.
delayed_consequences: Tests staff/successor investment made earlier.
A player who hoarded competence now has dramatically lower throughput.

chapters.title: LIQUIDITY
chapters.premise: If financial pressure is high, Meridian outflows accelerate; otherwise the same chapter becomes a credit-market freeze affecting Aster contractors.
required_beats: Central Bank knows more than government can safely publish.
Meridian's weakness is real but may be survivable.
One careless statement can become causal.
chapters.decision_gate: Design liquidity/backstop, disclosure and accountability sequence.
delayed_consequences: Financial stability can recover, require recapitalization, or become systemic crisis.
Kalen may survive, resign or lose control depending branch.

chapters.title: THE CONTRACT
chapters.premise: If energy dependency is high, Ordan uses renewal/volume terms during the crisis; otherwise the pressure takes the form of price shock or infrastructure bottleneck.
required_beats: Cheap supply can relieve households immediately.
Long lock-in increases future leverage.
Diversification capacity depends on Act II choices.
chapters.decision_gate: Use reserves, accept emergency terms, diversify at fiscal cost, or combine them.
delayed_consequences: Earlier optionality investments pay off—or their absence becomes visible.
Avera relationship determines how adversarial negotiation becomes.

chapters.title: THE LINE
chapters.premise: If labour trust is low, port/industrial action threatens Aster logistics; if high, labour becomes a stabilizing partner but demands a costly concession.
required_beats: The government can use emergency powers, bargain, or re-sequence operations.
Actors remember whether earlier promises were kept.
The material issue and status/dignity issue may differ.
chapters.decision_gate: Resolve the bottleneck without teaching either side that crisis hostage-taking always pays.
delayed_consequences: Can strengthen institutional bargaining or radicalize labor/political response.

chapters.title: THE SEA
chapters.premise: If maritime heat is high, a second incident places forces on alert; if low, Serrat offers joint de-escalation but domestic actors call it weakness.
required_beats: Intelligence cannot guarantee intent.
Both governments face domestic audience costs.
Private channel quality depends on Act IV.
chapters.decision_gate: Choose force posture, private contact, investigation and public red line.
delayed_consequences: Can create durable maritime mechanism, prolonged cold confrontation, or hard-failure escalation.

chapters.title: SEVENTY-TWO HOURS
chapters.premise: Government, markets and security systems all need decisions faster than normal process can comfortably provide.
required_beats: The player can request concentrated emergency authority, use distributed crisis cells, or rely on normal cabinet process.
Silas may offer operational cooperation while insisting on reciprocal oversight.
Elena evaluates not only whether the plan works but the precedent it creates.
chapters.decision_gate: Choose the architecture of crisis power.
delayed_consequences: This is the central test of institutional capacity.
If prior institutions are strong, distributed coordination can work.
If weak, concentration may save the immediate crisis but deepen personalized dependence.
Creates LEGACY_POWER_PRECEDENT.

acts.title: LEGACY
acts.time: Year 5 onward; recovery followed by a later transition window
acts.player_state: Potentially the most influential strategist in Lydria—or a damaged/outsider version of the same person.
acts.world_state: The crisis has revealed what the country actually built.
acts.central_question: What remains when your own power is no longer the answer?
